newsitem.title: USA: CITGO refinery fire shuts alkylation, other units.
newsitem.headline: CITGO refinery fire shuts alkylation, other units.

text.p: The fire at Citgo Petroleum Corp's Corpus Christi, Texas, refinery Monday night occurred in the alkylation unit and has shut that and other units at the plant, a spokesman for the company said Tuesday.
Production at the alkylation unit, with a rated capacity of 21,000 barrels per day (bpd), as well as some other units, has been taken down while the fire is allowed to burn out, the official said.
"It was the alkylation unit where the fire occured," said Kent Young, a spokesman for CITGO at its Tulsa, Okla., head office, though the cause of the initial explosion is still not determined.

"Some of the units were taken down last night. Whether they were able to block off areas and keep (some units) going, I can't say yet," Young added, though he didn't have details of which other units were affected.

The plant has a capacity to process 132,500 bpd of crude oil, with cat cracking of 77,000 bpd and reforming of 52,000 bpd (basically, gasoline production/enhancement). The alkylation unit makes blending components for gasoline.
The blast occured at 2222 CST/2322 EDT/0322 GMT Monday and rocked the local community.
Local emergency services personnel said Tuesday the fire would be allowed to burn out, a process that a police official said might take between 24 and 48 hours.
The cause of the explosion is still under investigation, local fire officials said.

"It is under investigation how it started. We didn't have any injuries. One of the private fire company employees was transferred to hospital for observation but that's it," said R.K. Gibson, assistant fire chief at Corpus Christi.

Gibson said it wasn't clear if the explosion was weather-related. "I had just gone to bed and it jarred the station really heavy. At first I thought it was a very loud clap of thunder but it was way to loud for that."
CITGO is a subsidiary of PDV America Inc, itself a division of state-owned Petroleos de Venezuela.
